results.text: Considering only orders with status 'delivered', list the product_category_name_english and the total price (summed across order_items) for that category, for the 5 categories with the highest total price.
results.generated_sql: SELECT t1.product_category_name_english, sum(t2.price) AS total_price FROM olist.product_category_name_translation AS t1 JOIN olist.products AS t3 ON t1.product_category_name = t3.product_category_name JOIN olist.order_items AS t2 ON t3.product_id = t2.product_id JOIN olist.orders AS t4 ON t2.order_id = t4.order_id WHERE t4.order_status = 'delivered' GROUP BY t1.product_category_name_english ORDER BY total_price DESC LIMIT 5
results.ground_truth_sql: SELECT t.product_category_name_english, sum(oi.price) AS total_revenue FROM olist.orders o JOIN olist.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN olist.products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN olist.product_category_name_translation t ON t.product_category_name = p.product_category_name WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' GROUP BY t.product_category_name_english ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, t.product_category_name_english LIMIT 5

results.text: List the seller_state and the number of DISTINCT customers (by customer_id) who bought an item from a seller in that state, for the 5 states with the most distinct customers.
results.generated_sql:
SELECT 
    s.seller_state AS seller_state, 
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS distinct_customers
FROM olist.sellers s
JOIN olist.order_items oi ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
JOIN olist.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY s.seller_state
ORDER BY distinct_customers DESC
LIMIT 5
results.ground_truth_sql: SELECT s.seller_state, count(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS distinct_customers FROM olist.sellers s JOIN olist.order_items oi ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id JOIN olist.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY s.seller_state ORDER BY distinct_customers DESC, s.seller_state LIMIT 5

results.text: Counting every individual review row (an order may have more than one review), list the customer_state and the number of reviews from that state, for the 5 states with the most reviews.
results.generated_sql:
SELECT 
    c.customer_state,
    COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count
FROM 
    olist.order_reviews r
JOIN 
    olist.orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN 
    olist.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY 
    c.customer_state
ORDER BY 
    review_count DESC
LIMIT 5
results.ground_truth_sql: SELECT c.customer_state, count(*) AS review_count FROM olist.customers c JOIN olist.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN olist.order_reviews r ON r.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_state ORDER BY review_count DESC, c.customer_state LIMIT 5

results.text: A REPEAT CUSTOMER is a customer_unique_id that placed more than one order. List the customer_unique_id and the total number of order_items across ALL of that customer's orders, for the 5 repeat customers with the most total order_items.
results.generated_sql:
SELECT 
    c.customer_unique_id, 
    COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_order_items
FROM olist.customers c
JOIN olist.orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN olist.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) > 1
ORDER BY total_order_items DESC
LIMIT 5
results.ground_truth_sql: SELECT c.customer_unique_id, count(oi.order_item_id) AS total_items FROM olist.customers c JOIN olist.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN olist.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE c.customer_unique_id IN (  SELECT customer_unique_id FROM olist.customers c2 JOIN olist.orders o2 ON o2.customer_id = c2.customer_id  GROUP BY customer_unique_id HAVING count(DISTINCT o2.order_id) > 1) GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id ORDER BY total_items DESC, c.customer_unique_id LIMIT 5

JOIN olist.product_category_name_translation t ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name

results.ground_truth_sql: SELECT count(*) AS sellers_without_bad_reviews FROM olist.sellers s WHERE NOT EXISTS (  SELECT 1 FROM olist.order_items oi JOIN olist.order_reviews r ON r.order_id = oi.order_id  WHERE oi.seller_id = s.seller_id AND r.review_score <= 2)

results.text: How many DISTINCT products (by product_id, among products that have been ordered at least once) have NEVER received an order_review scored below 3 on any order containing that product? Return a single count.

FROM olist.products AS p
JOIN olist.order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id

results.text: Using a window function, find the single highest-priced order_item in EACH product_category_name_english (partition by category, rank by price descending; if more than one item shares the highest price in a category, take the one with the LOWEST product_id). List the category, product_id and price for that top item, for the 5 categories whose top item has the highest price.
results.generated_sql: SELECT t.product_category_name_english, t.product_id, t.price FROM (SELECT c.product_category_name_english, i.product_id, i.price, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.product_category_name_english ORDER BY i.price DESC, i.product_id ASC) as rn FROM olist.order_items i JOIN olist.products p ON i.product_id = p.product_id JOIN olist.product_category_name_translation c ON p.product_category_name = c.product_category_name) t WHERE t.rn = 1 ORDER BY t.price DESC LIMIT 5
results.ground_truth_sql: WITH ranked AS (  SELECT t.product_category_name_english, oi.product_id, oi.price,         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.product_category_name_english ORDER BY oi.price DESC, oi.product_id) AS rn  FROM olist.order_items oi JOIN olist.products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id  JOIN olist.product_category_name_translation t ON t.product_category_name = p.product_category_name) SELECT product_category_name_english, product_id, price FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY price DESC, product_category_name_english LIMIT 5

results.text: Using a window function, for each review_score (1 through 5) list the review_score, the count of reviews with that score, and the CUMULATIVE percentage of all reviews at or below that score, rounded to 2 decimal places. Order by review_score ascending.
results.generated_sql:
SELECT 
    t.review_score,
    t.review_count,
    ROUND(SUM(t.review_count) OVER (ORDER BY t.review_score) * 100.0 / SUM(t.review_count) OVER (), 2) AS cumulative_percentage
FROM (
    SELECT 
        r.review_score,
        COUNT(*) AS review_count
    FROM olist.order_reviews r
    WHERE r.review_score IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY r.review_score
) t
ORDER BY t.review_score ASC
LIMIT 1000
results.ground_truth_sql: SELECT review_score, count(*) AS review_count, round(100.0 * sum(count(*)) OVER (ORDER BY review_score) / sum(count(*)) OVER (), 2) AS cumulative_pct FROM olist.order_reviews GROUP BY review_score ORDER BY review_score

results.text: Using a window function, find the single seller with the highest total order_item price (summed) within EACH seller_state (partition by state, rank by total price descending). List the seller_id, seller_state and that seller's total price, for the 5 states whose top seller has the highest total price.
results.generated_sql:
SELECT t.seller_id, t.seller_state, t.total_price
FROM (
    SELECT s.seller_id, s.seller_state, SUM(oi.price) AS total_price,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY s.seller_state ORDER BY SUM(oi.price) DESC) as rk
    FROM olist.sellers s
    JOIN olist.order_items oi ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
    GROUP BY s.seller_id, s.seller_state
) t
WHERE t.rk = 1
ORDER BY t.total_price DESC
LIMIT 5
results.ground_truth_sql: WITH ranked AS (  SELECT s.seller_id, s.seller_state, sum(oi.price) AS total_revenue,         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.seller_state ORDER BY sum(oi.price) DESC, s.seller_id) AS rnk  FROM olist.sellers s JOIN olist.order_items oi ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id  GROUP BY s.seller_id, s.seller_state) SELECT seller_id, seller_state, total_revenue FROM ranked WHERE rnk = 1 ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, seller_state LIMIT 5

results.text: For each order, compute its TOTAL payment_value (the sum of all payment records for that order -- some orders have more than one). Using a window function, find the single order with the highest total payment_value within EACH customer_state (partition by state). List the order_id, customer_state and that total payment_value, for the 5 states whose top order has the highest total payment_value.
results.generated_sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        o.order_id,
        c.customer_state,
        SUM(p.payment_value) AS total_payment_value
    FROM olist.orders o
    JOIN olist.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN olist.order_payments p ON o.order_id = p.order_id
    GROUP BY o.order_id, c.customer_state
),
ranked_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        ot.order_id,
        ot.customer_state,
        ot.total_payment_value,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ot.customer_state ORDER BY ot.total_payment_value DESC) as rn,
        MAX(ot.total_payment_value) OVER (PARTITION BY ot.customer_state) as max_state_payment
    FROM order_totals ot
)
SELECT 
    ro.order_id,
    ro.customer_state,
    ro.total_payment_value
FROM ranked_orders ro
WHERE ro.rn = 1
ORDER BY ro.max_state_payment DESC
LIMIT 5
results.ground_truth_sql: WITH order_totals AS (  SELECT o.order_id, c.customer_state, sum(op.payment_value) AS total_payment  FROM olist.orders o JOIN olist.customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id  JOIN olist.order_payments op ON op.order_id = o.order_id  GROUP BY o.order_id, c.customer_state), ranked AS (  SELECT order_id, customer_state, total_payment,         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_state ORDER BY total_payment DESC, order_id) AS rnk  FROM order_totals) SELECT order_id, customer_state, total_payment FROM ranked WHERE rnk = 1 ORDER BY total_payment DESC, customer_state LIMIT 5
